cover_alt: Two overlapping screens: the analytics home page and the full-screen AI Assistant chat creating a report.
summary: To empower clients to meet their own analytics needs, the business set out to design an AI-driven report authoring experience that reduces manual support demands and improves overall client satisfaction. This initiative aimed to simplify complex reporting tasks through intuitive AI assistance, giving clients greater control and confidence with their reports.

details.label: Role
items: Product design lead: Design direction and strategy
Guidance for designers, including a content designer and a researcher

blocks.text: Clients struggled to self-service access to their analytics around their employee experience, and over-reliance on client teams caused inefficiencies. High level pain points included:

items: Analytics were scattered across multiple platforms
Non-tech savvy users struggled with manually creating reports and dashboards
Clients’ ad-hoc requests resulted in delays, adding to client frustration

blocks.text: How can AI help clients with different technical skills get their analytics faster and easier, while decreasing the need for client team support?

items.title: Narrow Down the Scope
text: Focus on report capabilities: find, modify, create

items.title: GenAI Chat Experience
text: Intuitive conversational experience, regardless of level of data expertise

blocks.alt: Prototype still: the analytics home page with an Ask about reports button in the navigation.

blocks.text: I worked with the PM director and researcher to compile key questions about the clients’ use of analytics:

items: How do users currently use analytics?

items.text: Gather volume of responses to inform directional themes

items.lead: Interviews with clients and client teams
items.text: Understand details of their processes, goals, and pain points

blocks.alt: Snapshot of interview theming in Miro, with sticky notes grouped into themes.

items.title: Two User Types
list: Tactical: Use analytics for daily, weekly, or monthly tasks
Strategic: Use analytics to guide long-term plans

items.title: Heavy Report Usage
text: Most users were tactical, and they used reports more often than dashboards

items.title: Varied Level of Expertise
text: Some users can pull their own reports, while others require client team support

items.title: Backlogged Client Team Requests
text: As client requests piled up, client teams struggled with delivering requests on time

blocks.text: Based on the key insights, I partnered with the engineering lead to map out the user flow for the 3 main paths:

blocks.alt: User flow diagram for finding, editing, and creating a report with the AI assistant.

blocks.text: Choosing the AI assistant’s entry point was crucial, as it needed to be visually prominent, while setting user expectations on the specific reporting capabilities of the chat.

blocks.alt: Three entry point concepts. Rejected: a floating icon with unclear capabilities. Rejected: on the Reports page, which hides the feature. Selected: in navigation, a button with clear call-to-action text, accessible site-wide.

blocks.text: The chat window needed to scale to accommodate future functionality, including dashboards, report previews, and data visualizations. In collaboration with the engineering lead, we decided to design a scalable chat window upfront, rather than redesigning it in later phases.

blocks.alt: Three chat window concepts. Rejected: compact, too cramped for multi-step interactions. Rejected: side panel, limits embedded data visualizations. Selected: full takeover, which minimizes distractions and scales for embeds.

blocks.text: Design iterations for indicating AI-generated output focused on clarity and transparency. The pattern required distinguishing AI-generated content from standard chat responses, helping users immediately recognize when content had been created or modified by AI.

blocks.alt: Three AI output patterns. Rejected: report title only, too similar to a regular response. Rejected: a border that looks clunky. Selected: a solid background with icon and copy for strong visual differentiation.

blocks.text: As the AI assistant had functionality limited to reports, it was important to clearly indicate when users had finite paths to choose from, and where users could chat freely.

blocks.alt: Three conversation patterns: distinct paths with clear navigation, personalized suggestions based on interactions, and free form conversation with open-ended questions.

text: AI assistant set to roll out to 350+ clients across 3 domains (Leaves, Health, Wealth)
Set the foundation for AI-powered design patterns and chat voice and tone
Increased client self-service and reduced ad-hoc client team requests
Positive feedback from alpha and beta clients, rebuilding client trust

items.text: Although AI can support countless analytics processes, the team focused efforts on the priority use case of reports to deliver value where it mattered most

While the AI assistant supported conversational interactions, it was important to set user expectations around finite choices. Users needed to understand when they were navigating a limited set of options versus engaging in open-ended conversation with the assistant

items.lead: Limited client access for user feedback
items.text: The project faced challenges in recruiting client end users for feedback. I partnered with the Director of User Research and the Client Communications team to design and execute targeted recruitment efforts.
